notes.title: On Optimizing Top-K Metrics for Neural Ranking Models
notes.technique: Extends LambdaLoss with theoretically grounded weights for truncated metrics such as NDCG@K, replacing the original framework's top-k heuristic. ([research.google](https://research.google/pubs/on-optimizing-top-k-metrics-for-neural-ranking-models/?utm_source=openai))
notes.data: The paper supplies a top-k derivation and neural-ranking experiments on public learning-to-rank collections; KuaiRand transfer remains untested.
notes.effect: Best conceptual match for nDCG@5 and likely the strongest top-five reranking candidate. GAUC receives limited benefit because ordering below rank five is largely de-emphasized.
notes.cost: Pairwise list loss with cutoff masks; roughly LambdaLoss cost and practical for small reranking slates on CPU. Candidate scoring usually dominates inference cost.
notes.risk: Can ignore useful distinctions outside the cutoff, overfit sparse top-five labels, and cannot recover relevant items absent from the candidate set.
notes.applicability: Highest-priority 15-minute trial for KuaiRand nDCG@5. For joint optimization, blend it with a low-weight RankNet objective and select by validation GAUC plus nDCG@5.

notes.title: Set2setRank: Collaborative Set to Set Ranking for Implicit Feedback based Recommendation
notes.technique: Compares sampled positive and unobserved sets within each user, combining item-to-set separation with a set-level margin against the hardest sampled negative.
notes.data: Uses per-user observed and unobserved item sets, sampling L positives and K negatives. The paper supplies complexity analysis and component ablations.
notes.effect: Expected to improve top-k separation and nDCG@5 by exposing each positive to multiple negatives; GAUC alignment is useful but less direct than BPR.
notes.cost: Medium: reported complexity scales with interactions times K+L. Small sets are feasible, but harder than BPR within 15 minutes.
notes.risk: Hard negatives can be unobserved positives; users with very few positives cannot form informative sets. Results can be sensitive to K, L and margin weighting.
notes.applicability: A second-stage experiment after BPR/LambdaRank. Use tiny sets and cap hard-negative mining; otherwise the extra complexity is unlikely to justify the constrained trial.

notes.title: Contrastive Learning for Cold-Start Recommendation
notes.technique: CLCRec aligns content representations with collaborative user/item embeddings through contrastive objectives motivated by mutual-information maximization. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.05315?utm_source=openai))
notes.data: Evaluation explicitly separates warm and cold-start settings across four recommendation datasets and analyzes content–collaborative representation transfer.
notes.effect: Expected to improve both metrics on genuinely unseen items. GAUC benefits from better user–item separation; nDCG@5 may require an additional pairwise or top-weighted ranking loss.
notes.cost: Medium to high. A reduced-dimensional encoder, small sampled batches, and limited negatives are necessary for a 15-minute CPU trial.
notes.risk: False contrastive negatives, popularity leakage, and unstable loss weighting can erase gains; more tuning-sensitive than FM-based approaches.
notes.applicability: Use only after establishing a metadata-embedding baseline. Most relevant when the evaluation contains substantial item cold-start and content features are informative.

notes.title: Counteracting Duration Bias in Video Recommendation via Counterfactual Watch Time
notes.technique: Model watch time as right-censored by video duration and learn counterfactual watch-time interest with a censored likelihood.
notes.data: Training play time, duration, a full-play censoring indicator, and serving-time backbone features.
notes.effect: Targets GAUC and duration-segment stability, with indirect nDCG effects.
notes.cost: Medium-high because the custom likelihood adds sensitive distribution parameters.
notes.risk: Likelihood instability can consume the trial budget; use only a tiny head after simpler duration targets are exhausted.
notes.applicability: The EDA shows a material full-play share, matching the censoring formulation.

notes.title: Factorization Machines for Data with Implicit Feedback
notes.technique: FM-Pair combines factorization-machine feature interactions with the BPR pairwise objective for implicit feedback. Complexity scales linearly with active features. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.08254?utm_source=openai))
notes.data: Evidence covers implicit-feedback ranking with auxiliary contextual and cross-domain features.
notes.effect: Likely positive GAUC effect because BPR directly learns positive-versus-negative ordering. nDCG@5 gains may be smaller unless negatives are hard or position-weighted.
notes.cost: Low to medium. Suitable for sparse categorical KuaiRand features, small latent dimensions, and sampled pairs on CPU.
notes.risk: Unexposed items treated as negatives create exposure bias; unrestricted feature crosses or high-cardinality fields increase memory and overfitting.
notes.applicability: Strong CPU baseline for combining user, item, content, and context fields. Prefer sampled exposed non-clicks when available and emphasize hard negatives for nDCG@5.

notes.title: Automatic Expert Selection for Multi-Scenario and Multi-Task Search
notes.technique: AESM² stacks scenario-specialization layers below task-specialization layers and learns which shared or specialized experts each input should use.
notes.data: Evaluated on two industrial-scale datasets, with offline comparisons, component analysis, and an online deployment study. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14321?utm_source=openai))
notes.effect: Expected to improve segment-level GAUC by reducing majority-segment domination. It may improve nDCG@5 when scenario identity strongly changes item relevance.
notes.cost: High for the stated budget: multiple expert layers and learned selection add training overhead. A heavily reduced single-layer variant might fit; the full method is unlikely to finish a useful CPU trial in 15 minutes.
notes.risk: Selection instability, expert starvation, and over-specialization of small segments. More hyperparameters make short trials unreliable.
notes.applicability: Useful conceptual extension if KuaiRand segments represent distinct traffic scenarios. Less attractive than small MMoE under four CPU threads.

notes.title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
notes.technique: Use candidate-conditioned local activation over historical behavior embeddings.
notes.data: Strictly earlier ordered histories plus candidate and historical item metadata.
notes.effect: Targets user-specific GAUC and may lift top-five ranking when recent interests are supported.
notes.cost: High unless history length, embedding width, and attention depth are tightly bounded.
notes.risk: Earlier CPU implementations timed out or exceeded memory; exact-item histories are sparse.
notes.applicability: A tag-focused DIN-lite is more defensible than a full item sequence because prior user-tag support is 77.44%.

notes.title: DCN V2: Improved Deep and Cross Network and Practical Lessons for Web-scale Learning to Rank Systems
notes.technique: Learn explicit bounded-degree feature crosses with matrix or low-rank cross layers.
notes.data: Embedded categorical fields and normalized numerical context.
notes.effect: Targets both GAUC and nDCG through candidate-context interactions missed by FM.
notes.cost: Medium for one or two compact low-rank cross layers.
notes.risk: Large full-rank or mixture-of-expert variants exceed the CPU and memory envelope.
notes.applicability: A compact DCN residual is already strong locally; stabilization has higher value than architectural expansion.

notes.title: Uncovering User Interest from Biased and Noised Watch Time in Video Recommendation
notes.technique: D2Co models duration-conditioned watch-time mixtures and smooths correction parameters across nearby duration cohorts.
notes.data: Training watch time, duration, and optional engagement feedback for component diagnosis.
notes.effect: Targets GAUC and performance consistency across duration segments.
notes.cost: Medium if duration is quantized before fitting small mixture models.
notes.risk: Per-duration mixture fitting is fragile and more complex than D2Q or the existing RAD-style head.
notes.applicability: KuaiRand engagement outcomes can diagnose components, but only a corrected train-derived scalar may enter learning.

notes.title: Field-weighted Factorization Machines for Click-Through Rate Prediction in Display Advertising
notes.technique: Learn one scalar interaction strength per field pair while retaining one embedding per feature.
notes.data: Multi-field categorical user, item, context, and metadata features.
notes.effect: Targets personalized interaction quality and therefore primarily GAUC, with possible nDCG lift.
notes.cost: Low-to-medium parameter and CPU overhead relative to the rich FM backbone.
notes.risk: The prior full FwFM branch regressed; restrict any retry to an evidence-backed field-pair subset.
notes.applicability: Tag and duration crosses are plausible because user-tag history support is high while exact repeat-item support is low.

notes.title: Q(D)O-ES: Population-based Quality (Diversity) Optimisation for Post Hoc Ensemble Selection in AutoML
notes.technique: Maintains a population/archive of strong ensembles while explicitly preserving behavioral diversity, avoiding the single greedy path of standard ensemble selection.
notes.data: Evaluated across many heterogeneous prediction libraries with separate validation and test assessment; explicitly examines the interaction between quality, diversity and overfitting. ([proceedings.mlr.press](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v224/purucker23b.html))
notes.effect: May find a better GAUC/nDCG@5 trade-off when greedy selection repeatedly chooses near-duplicate models, but gains are less predictable than simple OOF stacking.
notes.cost: The paper’s full population search is outside the budget. A tiny archive and tens—not thousands—of candidate evaluations may fit 15 minutes.
notes.risk: Diversity optimization enlarges the search space and can overfit validation diversity without improving ranking quality.
notes.applicability: Medium. Use only as a second-stage search over a small shortlisted library; prioritize disagreement in top-five item order or per-user pairwise errors, not raw-score distance.

notes.title: RouteRec: Strict Evaluation of Recommender-Agent Selection and Aggregation
notes.technique: Uses leakage-free five-fold OOF predictions to compare request-level selection of one recommender with item-level learned aggregation of heterogeneous recommender scores.
notes.data: Methodological evidence comes from a strict fixed-candidate recommendation protocol contrasting routing and aggregation under identical OOF controls. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09908?utm_source=openai))
notes.effect: For KuaiRand, item-level regularized aggregation is more likely to improve nDCG@5 than hard per-user model routing; GAUC may improve through model-specific weights on each candidate.
notes.cost: A linear or ridge aggregator over precomputed scores is CPU-friendly. Exclude expensive agent or language-model components under the stated budget.
notes.risk: Meta-features can leak interaction labels; hard routing is statistically fragile when each user supplies limited supervision. Distribution shift between folds also destabilizes weights.
notes.applicability: High for an OOF stacker. Prefer item-level blending with fold-stable global weights; only add user-segment interactions when adequately regularized.

notes.title: Deep & Cross Network for Ad Click Predictions
notes.technique: The original DCN combines a cross network with an MLP. Each cross layer explicitly raises the maximum interaction degree by one while using a rank-constrained parameterization and residual connection. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.05123))
notes.data: Evidence includes sparse advertising CTR and dense classification tasks; the paper studies explicit bounded-degree crosses and memory efficiency, but not listwise recommendation metrics.
notes.effect: May improve GAUC and nDCG@5 when low-degree user–item–context conjunctions matter. Expected gains are smaller than DCN-V2 when interaction patterns require multiple independent projections.
notes.cost: Moderate but feasible with one or two cross layers and a very small MLP. Cross-layer cost is linear in concatenated embedding width; embedding tables remain the main RAM expense.
notes.risk: The original cross layer has restricted expressiveness. Extra depth can introduce unnecessary interactions, while the MLP increases runtime and tuning variance under a short trial.
notes.applicability: Useful as a lightweight bridge between FwFM and DCN-V2, especially if FwFM underfits. Keep the input width small and compare against FwFM before adding depth.

notes.title: Ensemble Selection from Libraries of Models
notes.technique: Original greedy ensemble selection: repeatedly add the candidate whose inclusion best improves a validation metric; repeated selection implicitly learns nonnegative weights. For KuaiRand, use leakage-free out-of-fold scores and optimize GAUC, nDCG@5, or a weighted combination directly.
notes.data: Evaluated with heterogeneous model libraries and multiple target metrics; establishes metric-specific post-hoc selection rather than score averaging. ([proceedings.mlr.press](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v18/balakrishnan12a/balakrishnan12a.pdf))
notes.effect: Expected small-to-moderate gain when base rankers have complementary errors; direct nDCG@5 selection can improve top-five ordering more than probability blending.
notes.cost: Very low after OOF predictions exist; practical within 15 minutes for roughly 5–30 models using streamed user groups.
notes.risk: Repeated validation decisions overfit, especially with many correlated candidates. Fold averaging, shallow selection and a minimum-improvement threshold are important.
notes.applicability: High. Use user- or time-aware folds, rank/quantile-normalize each model, and retain only models that improve both fold stability and the target metric.

notes.title: Learning to Rank with Non-Smooth Cost Functions (LambdaRank)
notes.technique: Scales RankNet pair gradients by the ranking-metric change caused by swapping the pair, concentrating updates on consequential positions. ([microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/learning-to-rank-with-non-smooth-cost-functions/?utm_source=openai))
notes.data: Provides an implicit-cost analysis and ranking experiments; evidence is from information retrieval rather than recommendation.
notes.effect: Directly targeting ΔnDCG@5 should improve top-five ordering more than plain RankNet. GAUC may be neutral or decline if low-ranked pairs receive little weight.
notes.cost: Sorting plus pair-delta computation; worst-case O(m²) per list. Feasible for short reranking slates, especially when pairs irrelevant to the cutoff are omitted.
notes.risk: Metric weights can be unstable with noisy labels or near-tied scores. Strong cutoff focus may damage global pairwise ordering and GAUC.
notes.applicability: High for KuaiRand reranking: use user/request lists and nDCG@5 swap weights. Retain a small RankNet term when GAUC is co-primary.

notes.title: DCN V2: Improved Deep & Cross Network and Practical Lessons for Web-scale Learning to Rank Systems
notes.technique: DCN-V2 replaces DCN's vector cross parameter with a matrix, enabling richer explicit interactions through stacked or parallel cross/deep branches. Its low-rank and mixture-of-experts variants trade expressiveness for efficiency; L cross layers represent interactions through degree L+1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.13535))
notes.data: Evidence spans synthetic polynomial interaction tests, public CTR/recommendation data, ablations, and first-party production learning-to-rank deployments. No direct KuaiRand or nDCG@5 evaluation is provided.
notes.effect: Highest potential GAUC and nDCG@5 lift of these methods when KuaiRand relevance depends on higher-order user–video–author–context crosses. Under the stated compute limit, realized gains may be small unless the low-rank form converges quickly.
notes.cost: Full-rank layers scale quadratically with input width and are unsuitable here. A one- or two-layer low-rank model with a tiny deep branch is plausible; a multi-expert mixture is risky within 3 GB RAM and 15 minutes.
notes.risk: Greater overfitting and tuning sensitivity than FwFM; full-rank matrices or multiple experts can exceed the budget. Pointwise loss may improve calibration without improving top-five ordering.
notes.applicability: Medium for the initial CPU trial, high for later scaling. Use low-rank cross layers, narrow embeddings, and a ranking-aligned loss or user-grouped sampling when nDCG@5 is the primary target.

notes.title: Learning to Rank using Gradient Descent (RankNet)
notes.technique: Pairwise logistic cross-entropy learns score differences between preferred and non-preferred items. ([microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/learning-to-rank-using-gradient-descent/?utm_source=openai))
notes.data: Evidence includes derivation plus experiments on query-grouped commercial search lists; no KuaiRand validation.
notes.effect: Strong alignment with GAUC when pairs are positive-versus-negative within each user group; only indirect improvement to nDCG@5 because all sampled pairs receive similar importance.
notes.cost: All-pairs training is O(m²) per candidate list. Pair sampling with a linear or tiny MLP scorer should fit four CPU threads, 3 GB RAM and a 15-minute trial.
notes.risk: Pair explosion, noisy ties, exposure bias and poor top-five emphasis. Uniform pair sampling can optimize GAUC while barely moving nDCG@5.
notes.applicability: Good inexpensive baseline and useful auxiliary loss. Group pairs by user/request; combine with a cutoff-aware loss if nDCG@5 is important.

notes.title: BPR: Bayesian Personalized Ranking from Implicit Feedback
notes.technique: Within each user group, applies a logistic pairwise loss so an observed item outranks a sampled unobserved item.
notes.data: Binary implicit interactions; requires user-level positive sets and negative sampling. Evidence includes a Bayesian derivation and applications to MF and kNN.
notes.effect: Expected to improve GAUC strongly because it learns within-user positive-versus-negative ordering; nDCG@5 gains are less direct because all sampled pairs receive similar importance.
notes.cost: Low: linear in sampled pairs and embedding dimension. MF-BPR is the safest fit for four CPU threads, 3 GB RAM and a 15-minute trial.
notes.risk: Unobserved items may be false negatives; uniform negatives can be too easy. The loss does not emphasize rank positions 1–5.
notes.applicability: Best baseline for KuaiRand GAUC. Sample pairs strictly within user, balance users rather than interactions, and consider moderately hard negatives.

notes.title: Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts
notes.technique: Foundational MMoE: shared dense experts are combined by separate learned gates for each prediction task. This is probably the original paper behind the query, although its gates are task-specific rather than segment-specific.
notes.data: Evidence comprises controlled synthetic task-relatedness experiments and a large-scale recommendation application with multiple objectives.
notes.effect: Likely improves GAUC when objectives or user segments need different representations while retaining useful sharing. nDCG@5 gains are indirect unless training adds ranking-aware weighting or loss.
notes.cost: Moderate. All experts execute for every example; a CPU trial should use 2–4 experts with narrow MLPs. Compatible with 3 GB RAM and potentially a 15-minute trial.
notes.risk: Expert redundancy, gate collapse, and negative transfer. Treating sparse segments as separate tasks can overfit or produce unstable GAUC estimates.
notes.applicability: Strong baseline for KuaiRand. Feed segment/context embeddings into each gate, but retain one ranking target unless segment sample sizes are large.

notes.title: VBPR: Visual Bayesian Personalized Ranking from Implicit Feedback
notes.technique: Extends BPR matrix factorization with user-specific preferences over a learned projection of pretrained item-content vectors. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.01784))
notes.data: The paper studies implicit interactions, large real-world collections, personalized ranking, and cold-start behavior using fixed visual descriptors.
notes.effect: Expected GAUC and nDCG@5 gains mainly when dense video/content vectors capture attributes users consistently prefer, especially for new items.
notes.cost: Medium with precomputed vectors; infeasible for the trial budget if feature extraction must also be performed. Reduce projection rank aggressively.
notes.risk: Weak or domain-mismatched content embeddings add noise; the original method is visual-specific and does not address exposure confounding.
notes.applicability: Conditional KuaiRand option if compact pretrained video/image descriptors already exist. Otherwise sparse metadata models are more practical.

notes.title: Heterogeneous Ranking in Industrial-Scale Recommender Systems: A Case Study
notes.technique: HA-MoE injects explicit heterogeneity or segment context into both gates and expert representations, directly targeting specialization and majority bias in heterogeneous ranking.
notes.data: Evidence includes industrial offline evaluation, specialization diagnostics, and online A/B testing in a heterogeneous feed. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27577?utm_source=openai))
notes.effect: Closest direct match for segment-aware GAUC optimization. Expected nDCG@5 benefit is strongest when segment context changes top-item ordering rather than merely click calibration.
notes.cost: Moderate to high as published. A feasible CPU approximation is 2–3 narrow experts, one small segment-conditioned gate, and no elaborate diagnostic machinery.
notes.risk: Recent industrial case study with limited direct transfer evidence for KuaiRand. Experts may simply memorize segment frequency; noisy segment labels can worsen ranking.
notes.applicability: Most literal architectural match. Test after MMoE, using coarse, sufficiently populated segments and reporting both overall and per-segment GAUC plus nDCG@5.

notes.title: Combining Predictors for Recommending Music: the False Positives’ Approach to KDD Cup Track 2
notes.technique: Combines heterogeneous collaborative-filtering, classification and ranking models. Greedy ensemble selection operates on each model’s per-user item ranks rather than incompatible raw scores, then projects the result to the required list structure.
notes.data: Direct recommender-ranking evidence using a large sparse music task; the paper explicitly studies diverse component models, validation-based selection and per-user rank aggregation. ([proceedings.mlr.press](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v18/balakrishnan12a/balakrishnan12a.pdf))
notes.effect: Rank normalization should help nDCG@5 when base-score calibration differs. GAUC benefits when models disagree usefully on within-user positive–negative ordering.
notes.cost: Ensemble fitting is lightweight; prediction storage dominates. Stream by user or retain compact ranks to stay below 3 GB.
notes.risk: The authors identify late-stage validation overfitting. Rank conversion also discards confidence margins that may matter for GAUC.
notes.applicability: Very high. Closest established template: create KuaiRand OOF predictions, convert scores to within-user percentile ranks, and greedily blend against a GAUC/nDCG@5 objective.

notes.title: Metadata Embeddings for User and Item Cold-start Recommendations
notes.technique: Hybrid matrix factorization: user/item vectors are sums of learned metadata-feature embeddings, trained with a sampled ranking loss such as WARP. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.08439))
notes.data: Evaluated under explicit cold-start, sparse-interaction, and warm regimes using user and item metadata.
notes.effect: Expected strongest improvement for cold/rare items. WARP is relatively aligned with nDCG@5; GAUC should improve when metadata predicts pairwise preference.
notes.cost: Low. Sparse features and 16–32-dimensional embeddings should permit a useful four-CPU, 15-minute trial.
notes.risk: No benefit for unseen feature values; noisy metadata can overwhelm collaborative signals. WARP sampling may become expensive late in training.
notes.applicability: Best first trial for KuaiRand: encode item content fields and optional user attributes as sparse features. Validate with chronological cold-item splits, not random interaction splits.

notes.title: Learning to Rank with Non-Smooth Cost Functions
notes.technique: Introduces LambdaRank: pairwise gradients are weighted by the target-metric change caused by swapping two items. Treat each user as a ranking group and use delta-nDCG@5 weights.
notes.data: Requires grouped candidate lists with binary or graded labels. The paper derives an implicit objective for otherwise non-differentiable ranking metrics.
notes.effect: Most directly aligned with nDCG@5; may also improve GAUC, although top-weighted updates can sacrifice some global pairwise consistency.
notes.cost: Medium. Enumerating every within-group pair is quadratic; restrict updates to positive-negative pairs and top-ranked candidates for a CPU trial.
notes.risk: Large groups cause pair explosion. Sparse groups or users without both label classes provide little signal; aggressive top-5 truncation can overfit noisy positives.
notes.applicability: Preferred objective when nDCG@5 is primary. A blend with unweighted BPR-style pair loss is safer when GAUC and nDCG@5 are jointly scored.

notes.title: Ensemble Selection from Libraries of Models
notes.technique: Greedily add diverse models according to held-out metric improvement while limiting selection overfit.
notes.data: Leakage-safe out-of-fold predictions from diverse model families.
notes.effect: Can balance GAUC and nDCG when component errors are complementary.
notes.cost: Low for blending after expensive component predictions already exist.
notes.risk: Public-validation weight search overfits; use coarse preregistered weights and an internal chronological holdout.
notes.applicability: Restrict to two or three self-generated, decorrelated exits and regenerate them inside the final candidate.

notes.title: The LambdaLoss Framework for Ranking Metric Optimization
notes.technique: Weight probabilistic pair losses by their effect on a target ranking metric such as nDCG.
notes.data: User groups, binary relevance labels, candidate scores, and observed within-user positive-negative pairs.
notes.effect: A Lambda@5 term directly targets nDCG@5 while a dominant BCE term preserves GAUC.
notes.cost: Medium with capped pairs per user and vectorized batches.
notes.risk: Pairwise-only fine-tuning already regressed; keep the ranking loss small and in the same update as BCE.
notes.applicability: Use user_id as the query and only observed short-view impressions as negatives.

notes.title: Deconfounding Duration Bias in Watch-time Prediction for Video Recommendation
notes.technique: D2Q converts watch time to a train-fitted within-duration-group empirical quantile target.
notes.data: Training play time, duration, and ordinary serving-time features.
notes.effect: A cleaner duration-relative interest auxiliary is expected to help GAUC and duration-segment stability.
notes.cost: Low when quantile labels are cached and predicted by a tiny shared auxiliary head.
notes.risk: Published watch-time objectives do not directly guarantee binary long-view GAUC or nDCG gains.
notes.applicability: The schema has training play_time_ms and serving-time duration_ms; no validation outcome is required.

notes.title: LightGCN: Simplifying and Powering Graph Convolution Network for Recommendation
notes.technique: Propagate and average user-item embeddings over a normalized implicit-feedback graph without feature transforms.
notes.data: A train-only user-item positive graph and observed or sampled ranking pairs.
notes.effect: Primarily targets warm-user and warm-item GAUC.
notes.cost: High under the current CPU envelope even with shallow propagation.
notes.risk: Sparse repeat-video support and a prior timeout/weak repair make this a low-priority diversity branch.
notes.applicability: Only reconsider as a shallow residual if diagnostics show collaborative signal beyond the strong tag history.
